intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that pyridoxine-refractory autosomal recessive sideroblastic anemia-2 (SIDBA2) is caused by mutation in the SLC25A38 gene, which encodes an erythroid-specific mitochondrial carrier family protein; Guernsey et al. (2009) defined this autosomal recessive nonsyndromic form of congenital sideroblastic anemia by positional cloning.

checks.evidence_quote: we define a previously unknown form of autosomal recessive nonsyndromic congenital sideroblastic anemia, associated with mutations in the gene encoding the erythroid specific mitochondrial carrier family protein SLC25A38
checks.explanation: The abstract supports an autosomal recessive sideroblastic anemia caused by SLC25A38 mutations. It never says the disorder is pyridoxine-refractory, so that detail is not supported by the abstract.

paragraphs.text: The sideroblastic anemias are a heterogeneous group of congenital and acquired hematologic disorders. Their morphologic hallmark is the presence of ringed sideroblasts, which are bone marrow erythroid precursors with pathologic iron deposits within mitochondria (Guernsey et al., 2009). SIDBA2 is an autosomal recessive, nonsyndromic congenital form caused by mutation in the SLC25A38 gene (Guernsey et al., 2009). Affected individuals have had transfusion-dependent anemia from birth that did not respond to pyridoxine (Jardine et al., 1994).

checks.explanation: The abstract supports this. The label SIDBA2 is standard nomenclature.

checks.evidence_quote: A son and daughter of unaffected parents had transfusion dependent, pyridoxine-refractory sideroblastic anaemia from birth.
checks.explanation: The abstract describes only two affected sibs. It does not mention SIDBA2 or SLC25A38, so the generalization to all individuals with SIDBA2 goes beyond this paper.

checks.explanation: Pyridoxine-refractory anemia is reported only in these two sibs. The generalization to SIDBA2 as a defined entity does not come from this paper.

paragraphs.text: In the female infant reported by Manabe et al. (1982), erythroblast delta-aminolevulinic acid (ALA) synthetase activity was markedly reduced, both with and without pyridoxal phosphate. Erythroblast mitochondrial neutral protease activity, which specifically inactivates the apo form of ALA synthetase, was normal, and the sensitivity of apo-ALA synthetase to this protease was also normal. The authors speculated that the low ALA synthetase activity resulted from impaired production of the enzyme rather than rapid destruction, and that this could explain the lack of response to pyridoxine.

paragraphs.text: Jardine et al. (1994) concluded that pyridoxine-refractory congenital sideroblastic anemia in a family with an affected brother and sister born to unaffected parents was an autosomal recessive trait. The affected sibs had inherited different maternal alleles at the ALAS2 locus, and the mother was shown not to carry an X-linked sideroblastic anemia mutation. Guernsey et al. (2009) defined an autosomal recessive nonsyndromic congenital sideroblastic anemia caused by mutations in SLC25A38.

paragraphs.text: Jardine et al. (1994) excluded the erythroid-specific ALAS2 gene on Xp11.21 as the cause of sideroblastic anemia in a brother and sister. Sequencing of ALAS2 in the brother found no mutations in the coding region, the intron/exon boundaries, or the 1-kb 5-prime promoter region. The authors identified a G-to-A transition 220 nt 3-prime of the AATAAA polyadenylation signal; in an analysis of 148 alleles by mismatch PCR and XmnI restriction digestion, this polymorphism had a gene frequency of 25%. Analysis of this intragenic polymorphism showed that the affected sibs had received different maternal alleles at the ALAS2 locus. In addition, the mother did not have a dimorphic erythrocyte population and showed random X inactivation in peripheral leukocytes, indicating that she did not carry an X-linked sideroblastic anemia mutation.

paragraphs.text: Using positional cloning, Guernsey et al. (2009) identified mutations in the SLC25A38 gene, which encodes an erythroid-specific mitochondrial carrier family protein, in patients with autosomal recessive nonsyndromic congenital sideroblastic anemia. They also showed that SLC25A38 is important for heme biosynthesis in eukaryotes. The abstract did not give the specific mutations or the number of patients.

agent.process_note: I read all three papers, but each was available only as an abstract. SLC25A38 was established as the causal gene with autosomal recessive inheritance by Guernsey et al. (2009). That abstract does not give the specific mutations, their zygosity (homozygous vs compound heterozygous), the number of patients or families, or their ancestry, so no allelic variants were listed. No HGNC reference data were supplied, so the gene MIM number and chromosomal location of SLC25A38 were left out. Jardine et al. (1994) provided the ALAS2 exclusion and the evidence for recessive inheritance. Manabe et al. (1982) provided the biochemical findings in a single female infant.
